newsitem.title: USA: MSRB to seek more disclosure on derivatives deals.
newsitem.headline: MSRB to seek more disclosure on derivatives deals.

text.p: The MSRB voted to propose that underwriters and financial advisers disclose key information to state and local government clients when handling their swaps and other derivatives deals, the panel announced on Monday.

The Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board decided at a quarterly meeting April 30 - May 1 to seek an amendment to an existing rule that would require dealers for the first time to disclose whether they were acting as principals in derivatives transactions and whether they got any payments from or gave payments to any other parties to the deals.

The board's action follows last August's criminal conviction of former Lazard Freres & Co banker Mark Ferber for failing to tell financial advisory clients about a fee splitting arrangement with Merrill Lynch & Co Inc . concerning swaps transactions.

The upcoming amendments, which the panel plans to propose before the end of May, also would require financial advisers to disclose whether they acted as principal in a derivatives deal and whether they received any payment from a third party, the board said.

The board's rule would not affect independent financial advisers. But the board said it will urge municipal market groups voluntarily to set a high disclosure standard for all transactions, including non-dealer financial advisers.
The board said it will meet with the Government Finance Officers Association and the National Association of Independent Public Finance Advisors on the issue.

"While these proposed amendments only apply to registered broker-dealers, we think a higher standard should apply in all underwritings," MSRB Chairman Roger Hayes said at Monday's telephone briefing with reporters.
